title: What are T Levels?
content: T Levels are a Level 3 qualification designed for students aged 16 to 19. They combine classroom study with a substantial industry placement and are intended to help students move into skilled employment, apprenticeships or further study. T Levels are designed to give students a strong technical foundation while retaining the broad educational value of a post-16 qualification.

title: How T Levels are structured
content: A T Level usually includes classroom learning, practical technical study and an industry placement. The qualification is intended to provide a route that is more applied than a purely academic route and gives students employer-facing experience as part of their learning.

title: T Levels compared with A Levels
content: T Levels are a different route from A Levels. A Levels are generally more academic and are often chosen by students who want to continue into higher education, while T Levels are designed to be a more technical and applied option with stronger links to industry and work-based learning.

title: Who T Levels are for
content: T Levels are aimed at students who want a practical route into a technical career or further study. They are particularly suitable for students who prefer applied learning, technical subjects and a stronger connection between classroom study and the workplace.

title: Progression after T Levels
content: Students can progress into skilled employment, apprenticeships, higher technical study or university depending on their subject and next steps. The qualification is designed to support progression into work and further training while providing a strong technical foundation.

title: Ada College sixth form experience
content: At Ada, learning goes beyond the classroom. Students work on real-world projects, gain hands-on experience and learn directly from industry experts. The college emphasises practical skills, problem-solving, creativity and collaboration, all of which are valued by employers in digital and technology sectors.

title: Support and access
content: Ada offers support such as free laptops, bursaries and travel support where needed to help students succeed. This matters because students should be able to access the programme and take advantage of the practical learning opportunities without being prevented by cost or access barriers.

title: Ada and digital career pathways
content: Ada is a specialist digital and technology college. For students interested in digital careers, software, creative technology, problem-solving and technical work, a T Level route can align closely with industry-led learning and employer-facing practice.

title: Student support and guidance
content: Ada provides learner services and support to help students navigate the education experience. This includes practical support and guidance so students can make informed decisions about their study path, academic progress and career direction.

title: Technical route into employment and study
content: T Levels are intended to provide a technical route into employment and further study. They are designed for students who want a qualification that combines academic rigour with practical skills and a clearer link to workplace expectations.
